newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Yen, Sfr continue to dominate Hungary FX futures.
newsitem.headline: Yen, Sfr continue to dominate Hungary FX futures.

text.p: Yen and Swiss franc futures continued to dominate Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) trade on Friday, while turnover on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) was negligible, traders said.
The BCE's financial section posted turnover of 6.54 billion forints ($37 million), while currency futures turnover on the BSE totalled just 16.9 million forints.

Long-term yen and Swiss franc contracts, mainly September and December, accounted for more than half the almost 40,000 lots traded on the BCE. The mark, which maintained its spot value against the dollar, was also popular.
"The Swiss franc and yen, with their low interest rates, continue to offer a good long-term bet in tandem with a forint whose future devaluation is predetermined," one dealer said.
The forint is devalued by 1.2 percent per month -- to be reduced to 1.1 percent in April -- against a currency basket made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar.
Swiss francs closed firmer for March but down for all other maturities while the Japanese yen fell in all months. The mark rose for September and December.
On the BSE, there were just two trades for September marks, which strengthened the September price by 35 fillers to 112.5 forints. All other prices remained unchanged.
